clue.text: Firm order initially put in by one working with horses

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
something put in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the next

blocks.note: firm and steady
taken as written; it holds the next piece
first letter of order

explanation.surface: A company instruction is first handed to someone who looks after horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' does double duty in the surface, but cryptically it is a literal word with O put in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stableboy is a young groom who tends horses in a stable.

clue.text: Endless criticism involving old philosopher

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the word is cut off
involving means taking something in, so the shortened word wraps around another piece

blocks.note: informal word for harsh criticism, as in 'take some stick'
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker faces non-stop criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: STICK loses its K to become STIC, which then wraps around O. 'Stick' meaning criticism is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of the ancient Greek school founded by Zeno, so an old philosopher.

clue.text: Surprise caused by a tanker originally entering channel

indicators.note: originally refers to how a word begins, so its first letter is taken
a letter entering something goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a sound is a narrow sea channel
first letter of tanker

explanation.surface: An oil tanker sailing into a strait causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to surprise greatly, a stronger synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Deliberately ignore fashion article on alternative fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the words before it come first in the grid

blocks.note: a look is a style in fashion
the definite article
the other option
fashion as in manner: in this way

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately disregards one fashion feature in favour of another style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' appears twice with two senses: a style of dress and a manner of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To look the other way is the idiom for choosing to ignore wrongdoing.

clue.text: Engagement later - both made up

indicators.note: something made up is invented or put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple who quarrelled later make up and get engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' reads as reconciling after a row, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal promise to marry, an engagement.

clue.text: Long period of time before end of depression

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a year is a period of time
last letter of depression

explanation.surface: A long spell of time passes before depression finally lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the period, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Chaplain may give tramp religious education

blocks.note: to pad is to walk or tramp along
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A chaplain might offer a homeless person some religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' suggests a vagrant, but here it is the verb to trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a military or institutional chaplain.

clue.text: Go on a pub crawl, to get rid of the blues?

definitions.text: Go on a pub crawl, to get rid of the blues?

blocks.note: surface reading: go out drinking and celebrating wildly

blocks.clueFragment: to get rid of the blues?
blocks.note: setter's reading: cover a blue-coloured town in another colour of paint

explanation.walkthrough: 'the blues' means low spirits for the reveller, but literally a blue colour that a fresh coat of crimson paint would cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out and celebrate boisterously, typically drinking in many bars.

clue.text: Tramp carrying one collection of papers

indicators.note: one who carries something holds it within, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vagrant is carrying a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for a tramp, someone who dosses down wherever they can.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents gathered on one subject or person.

clue.text: Film starring Jessie Matthews - about parting revenge, roughly

indicators.note: a piece parting a word splits it apart by sitting in the middle
roughly means approximately, not in exact order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an old film's plot: a tale of rough revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Evergreen (1934) was a British musical starring Jessie Matthews, the stage and screen star of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen is the title of a 1934 British musical film whose leading lady was Jessie Matthews.

clue.text: Chooses not to be involved with new post abroad

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
abroad in the sense of out and about, widely circulating

explanation.surface: Someone declines a fresh job posting overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' suggests a foreign country, but here means out, as news is abroad when it is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part, a phrasal verb in the third person.

clue.text: A series in dispute

blocks.note: taken as written
a tissue is a connected series, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: A sequence of things is contested.
explanation.walkthrough: The split is A + TISSUE, not AT + ISSUE as the enumeration suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being argued over or contested.

clue.text: Have no influence getting foreign noble free

blocks.note: a count is a European nobleman, the continental equivalent of an earl
for nothing means without charge

explanation.surface: A powerless person lets a foreign aristocrat go free.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that counts for nothing has no weight or value in deciding matters.

clue.text: Grasslike plant in small border

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A garden plant growing in a narrow flowerbed edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grasslike plant of wet ground, from the family Cyperaceae.

clue.text: Drink stewed tea in ward, so busy

indicators.note: stewed means cooked to a mush, so the letters lose their order
busy suggests bustling movement, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a busy hospital ward, stewed tea is the drink on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'stewed' and 'busy' shuffle their neighbours, so all nine letters of tea, ward and so are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated water drunk alone or as a mixer.

clue.text: US author may, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or said, so we go by the sound of a word

blocks.note: may is the blossom of a common hedge shrub

explanation.surface: An American writer might, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb, but it is the hedge tree whose blossom appears in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was the American novelist who wrote The Scarlet Letter.

clue.text: Started and took the lead

blocks.note: first meaning: began or proceeded
second meaning: moved in front of the others

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a race report, but the two halves are separate senses of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to proceed with a plan and to move into first place.

clue.text: Athletic event last month, Irish town shortened

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the last month
Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands

explanation.surface: A sports event held last December in a small Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is a ten-event athletics competition.

clue.text: Tweet from Greek character, leading bishop inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so this piece sits between the others

blocks.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
up means ahead, as a team leading is two goals up

explanation.surface: A social media post from a Greek figure, with a senior bishop involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests social media, but it is a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a short bird call, the sound of a tweet.

clue.text: After short time, warning device may become a source of irritation

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a car horn sounds a warning

explanation.surface: After a while, a car horn becomes an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short time' means the abbreviation of time; 'after' places HORN behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is a persistent annoyance, so a thorn is a source of irritation.

clue.text: Work in front of ironmonger's, on view

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is kept

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
first letter of ironmonger's
taken as written

explanation.surface: Goods displayed in front of a hardware shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: An ironmonger is a British hardware shop. 'view' looks like display, but is the definition: a point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is one's view or judgement on a matter.

clue.text: Never doing anything wrong, chess player threw in hat excitedly

indicators.note: doing something excitedly is wild and disorderly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: White is the player with the white pieces
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess player excitedly tosses in a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone morally spotless, from an old detergent advertising slogan.

clue.text: Actor O'Toole, at heart, soft-hearted

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its middle, with the outer letters stripped away
having something as its heart means it is placed in the centre

blocks.note: O'Toole with its outer letters removed
p for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: The actor Peter O'Toole was, deep down, a softie.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaim Topol was the Israeli actor famed as Tevye in Fiddler on the Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Topol was the stage name of Israeli actor Chaim Topol.

clue.text: Bird dog dropping first of birds

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word
dropping means letting go of, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
first letter of birds

explanation.surface: A hunting dog drops the first bird it has retrieved.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Resign from bank at Oxford on Thursday?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is written after it, so the earlier words follow the day

blocks.note: Th is the abbreviation for Thursday
a bank is a row, as of keys or oars
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job at a bank in Oxford on a Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means in residence there as a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw up a job or post is to give it up, so it means resign.

clue.text: Making a mistake about a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: erring means making a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone errs over an item of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is an ornament worn on the ear, a type of jewellery.

clue.text: Salesman's extremely lengthy answer

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes of a word, its two ends

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative; the 's is read as 'is' joining it on
the first and last letters of lengthy

explanation.surface: A salesman gives a very long-winded answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely lengthy' looks like very long, but means only the end letters of lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is an answer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Messed about, ace landed upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flying ace was upset after landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messed about' is past tense, matching LED in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone a dance is an idiom for causing them trouble by being evasive, messing them about.
